feedback: Pre-race review of the iteration 4 candidate. It keeps the iteration 1 design, the best raced result at 178.2, and changes one variable: base_speed 1.3 to 1.1. Geometry (five sensors at x = ±0.03, ±0.015, 0; 12 mm footprints), sensor_weights [2,1,0,-1,-2], kp 2.5, kd 0.3, ki 0 and last_direction are unchanged. Iteration 2 showed that widening the array to 22.5 mm spacing did not improve line retention (line_loss_events stayed at 1.0, score 81.1), so the narrow layout is correct. Iteration 1 averaged 1.25 line-loss events on the oval and 1.9 on the s-bend, with max_error about 0.061 to 0.063 m against the 0.06 m off-track limit. Since each line-loss event removes about 15 points per unit of progress, a speed change that keeps the line is worth testing. Iteration 3 showed that kp 2.2 with kd 0.25 scored lower (106.7), so the kp/kd change of that iteration should not be reintroduced without a separate test. The candidate is valid and not obviously broken. It is also a clean single-variable test of the best raced design, and the iteration count leaves room to learn from it, so it is approved for the race. Interpreting the next race: if line_loss_events remain at 1 or more and max_error stays near 0.06, the next revision should try base_speed about 0.9 with gains held. If runs finish with line loss near zero but completion_time is above 3.0 s, base_speed should go back up toward 1.2 to 1.3, since iteration 1 finished the oval in about 1.97 s at 1.3. If oscillation stays above about 0.3 on the oval with line loss already low, lower kd to about 0.25 as a separate step.
requested_changes: If line_loss_events stay at 1 or more and max_error stays near 0.06, lower base_speed to about 0.9 and hold the narrow geometry, kp 2.5, kd 0.3, since iteration 1 at 1.3 and iteration 4 at 1.1 are the only controlled comparisons of speed.
If runs finish with line_loss_events near 0 but completion_time is above 3.0 s, raise base_speed to about 1.2 to 1.3 and hold kp and kd, since iteration 1 finished the oval at about 1.97 s.

If steering_oscillation stays above about 0.3 on the oval once line loss is low, lower kd to about 0.25 by itself, since iteration 1 (kd 0.3) gave 0.34 on the oval and iteration 3 (kd 0.25 with kp 2.2) gave 0.14 but also lost the line.
